title: Claude
content:
## Overview

Claude is Anthropic's family of large language models known for extended context windows, strong reasoning capabilities, and careful instruction-following. Emergent natively supports Claude models through the **Universal LLM Key**, allowing you to use Claude for code generation, chat interactions, and other AI-powered features throughout the platform.

<Note>
Claude models are available on all Emergent plans. Your usage is metered through your Universal LLM Key balance.
</Note>

## Supported Models

Emergent currently supports the following Claude model families:

| Model | Context Window | Best For |
|-------|----------------|----------|
| Claude 3.5 Sonnet | 200K tokens | Code generation, complex reasoning, detailed documentation |
| Claude 3 Opus | 200K tokens | Highest-quality outputs, nuanced understanding |
| Claude 3 Sonnet | 200K tokens | Balanced performance and speed |
| Claude 3 Haiku | 200K tokens | Fast responses, simple tasks |

Model availability and naming may be updated as Anthropic releases new versions. Emergent automatically maps to the latest stable releases.

## Setting Up Claude

<Steps>
<Step title="Ensure you have LLM credits">
Claude models consume credits from your Universal LLM Key balance. Check your current balance in **Settings → Billing** or by clicking your profile icon.

If you need to add credits, see [The Universal LLM Key](/the-universal-llm-key) for top-up instructions.
</Step>

<Step title="Select Claude in the model picker">
When starting a new conversation or editing an existing agent's configuration, open the **model picker** dropdown. Claude models appear under the "Anthropic" provider section.

Choose the model that best fits your use case—`Claude 3.5 Sonnet` is recommended for most code generation tasks.
</Step>

<Step title="Start building">
Describe your app, feature, or question as you normally would. Emergent's agents will use Claude to interpret your request, generate code, write tests, and deploy your application.
</Step>
</Steps>

## When to Use Claude

Claude excels in scenarios requiring:

- **Long-context understanding** — Claude can process large codebases, extensive documentation, or multi-file diffs in a single prompt.
- **Nuanced instruction-following** — Complex requirements with many constraints are handled reliably.
- **Safety-conscious outputs** — Claude is designed to refuse unsafe or problematic requests, reducing the risk of generating vulnerable code.

<Tip>
If you're working on a project with detailed domain logic or intricate state management, Claude 3.5 Sonnet often produces cleaner, more maintainable code than smaller or faster models.
</Tip>

## Switching Between Models Mid-Conversation

You can change models at any point during a conversation:

1. Click the **model badge** in the conversation header.
2. Select a different Claude variant (or switch to another provider entirely).
3. Continue chatting—subsequent messages will use the newly selected model.

Previous messages remain unchanged; only new responses reflect the updated model choice.

## Cost and Rate Limits

- **Pricing** is based on tokens consumed (input + output). Emergent's Universal LLM Key pricing includes a small markup over Anthropic's API rates to cover infrastructure and aggregation.
- **Rate limits** are managed automatically. If you hit a temporary quota, Emergent will queue your request and retry, or you can manually retry after a brief wait.

Check your **Usage Dashboard** under Settings to monitor token consumption by model and conversation.

<Warning>
Claude models with extended context windows can consume credits quickly when processing very large inputs. Review your prompt size if costs are higher than expected.
</Warning>

## Context Window Best Practices

Claude's 200K-token context is powerful, but here's how to make the most of it:

- **Include full file contents** when asking for refactors or debugging—Claude can handle the entire codebase context.
- **Provide examples** of desired output formats; Claude learns patterns from in-context demonstrations.
- **Avoid repetition** if possible; Claude retains conversation history well, so you don't need to re-explain setup in every message.

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Claude responses are slower than expected">
Larger models (Opus, Sonnet) prioritize quality over speed. If you need faster iteration, try **Claude 3 Haiku** for simpler tasks, then switch back to Sonnet for final polish.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Model returns 'overloaded' errors">
Anthropic's API occasionally experiences high demand. Emergent will automatically retry. You can also manually retry the message or switch to another model temporarily.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Unexpected refusals or overly cautious responses">
Claude is trained to decline potentially unsafe requests. If you believe a refusal is incorrect, rephrase your prompt to clarify intent, or try a different model for comparison.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
